Have you heard of Baba Yaga?

Top 5 things to know about the Slavic forest witch:

1) Baba Yaga is a supernatural old woman in Slavic folklore who lives deep in the forest and may help or eat those who find her.

2) Her hut is famously said to stand on chicken legs and to turn to face visitors when they speak the right words.

3) She flies in a mortar, steering with a pestle, and sweeps her trail away with a broom.

4) In many tales she sets impossible tasks for heroes; pass and she may give a gift, fail and you become dinner.

5) She appears across Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, and other Slavic story cycles as both villain and ambiguous threshold guardian.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baba_Yaga
posts.headline: Have you heard of Baba Yaga?

posts.text:
Have you heard of the kappa?

Top 5 things to know about Japan's river imp:

1) The kappa is a water creature from Japanese folklore, usually said to live in rivers and ponds across the country.

2) Classic art shows a child-sized humanoid with webbed hands and feet, a turtle-like beak or shell, and a water-filled dish on top of its head.

3) Folklore says the dish is its weak spot: bow to a kappa and it will politely bow back, spilling the water and losing its strength.

4) Stories credit kappa with both drowning the unwary and, in friendlier tales, teaching humans bone-setting and irrigation tricks.

5) Kappa remain a pop-culture staple in Japan, from shrine statues to warning signs near swimming holes.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa
posts.headline: Have you heard of the kappa?

posts.text:
Have you heard of La Llorona?

Top 5 things to know about Latin America's Weeping Woman:

1) La Llorona, the Weeping Woman, is a ghost legend told across Mexico and much of Latin America: a woman who drowned her children and now wanders crying for them.

2) Parents use the story as a warning to keep children away from rivers and dangerous water after dark.

3) Some historians link parts of the legend to older Aztec omens, including the goddess Cihuacoatl said to weep in the night before the Spanish conquest.

4) Colonial-era tellings blended Indigenous and European ghost motifs into the mother-who-killed-her-children tale known today.

5) She is sometimes connected in popular culture with La Malinche, though scholars treat that as later symbolic reading, not a single historical origin.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Llorona
posts.headline: Have you heard of La Llorona?

posts.text:
Have you heard of the Anakim?

Top 5 things to know about the biblical giant clan:

1) The Anakim are a people the Hebrew Bible describes as exceptionally tall, descended from Anak, and living in the hill country around Hebron.

2) In Numbers 13, the Israelite spies say they felt like grasshoppers beside the Anakim and link them to the Nephilim.

3) Deuteronomy and Joshua say Joshua and Caleb drove the Anakim from the hill country; a remnant is said to remain in Philistine cities including Gath.

4) They are often grouped with other giant peoples labeled Rephaim, Emim, and Zamzummim in the conquest narratives.

5) Later Jewish and Christian tradition kept reading them as historical giants who stood in the way of Israel's entry into the land.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anakim
posts.headline: Have you heard of the Anakim?

posts.text:
Have you heard of Cadborosaurus?

Top 5 things to know about the Pacific Northwest's sea serpent:

1) Cadborosaurus, or Caddy, is a sea-serpent cryptid reported along the coasts of British Columbia and the U.S. Pacific Northwest, named after Cadboro Bay near Victoria.

2) Witnesses usually describe a long serpentine body with vertical humps, flippers, and a horse- or camel-like head.

3) Sightings surged in the 1930s after newspapers in Victoria popularized the name Caddy.

4) In 1937 a Naden Harbour whaling station reported a strange carcass; decades later researchers Paul LeBlond and Edward Bousfield used such accounts in a controversial 1995 paper proposing the name Cadborosaurus willsi.

5) Skeptics often argue misidentified sharks, oarfish, or other marine animals; no live specimen has been confirmed.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadborosaurus
posts.headline: Have you heard of Cadborosaurus?

Answer: B) Wendigo

In Algonquian traditions across the northern forests of Canada and the northern United States, the Wendigo (or Windigo) is a cannibal spirit tied to winter, famine, and greed. Stories warn that a person who resorts to cannibalism, or who lets hunger and selfishness take over, can become one. Modern pop culture often adds antlers; older accounts describe an emaciated, ice-hearted giant instead.

How'd you do?
posts.headline: Answer: B) Wendigo

Near Huffman, Texas, northeast of Houston. Night of December 29, 1980, about 9 p.m.

Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum, and Vickie's seven-year-old grandson Colby are driving home on a rural two-lane road through pine woods when a huge diamond-shaped object appears low over the trees. It vents flame from its underside and throws off intense heat.

Cash stops the Oldsmobile. She and Vickie get out. The door handle is too hot to touch. When the object rises, they count roughly twenty-three helicopters around it, including twin-rotor Chinooks.

Within hours all three are sick. Burns, vomiting, hair loss. Cash is hospitalized. They later sue the federal government. The case is dismissed. The object never gets an official name.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cash%E2%80%93Landrum_incident
posts.headline: Near Huffman, Texas, northeast of Houston. Night of December 29, 1980, about 9 p.m.

Uintah County, Utah, on a remote cattle ranch later nicknamed Skinwalker Ranch. Between 1994 and 1996, Terry and Gwen Sherman tell a local reporter what they have been living with on their roughly five-hundred-acre spread near Fort Duchesne.

Crop circles. UFOs. Cattle cut up in a clean, bloodless, almost surgical way. And animals that should not be there, including a wolf they put at three times normal size. Terry says he shot it at close range with a rifle and it kept going as if the rounds did nothing.

Within months of the story hitting print in June 1996, Las Vegas businessman Robert Bigelow buys the ranch and brings in round-the-clock researchers. The Uinta Basin already had a reputation as UFO Alley. The Shermans' eighteen months put a name on the map.

Source: https://www.history.com/articles/skinwalker-ranch-paranormal-ufos-mutilation

Settle, North Yorkshire, England. March 2026. Video game developer Willow Hunter has lived in his flat about seven months when doors start opening and closing on their own. He blames a draft. Then his cat Kari refuses to go downstairs.

He sets up living-room CCTV. The camera catches a child's toy slowly wheeling out of frame while his daughter plays on the floor, and a skateboard clattering down by itself. Moments later she runs upstairs saying someone was in the room with her. Other clips show a teddy bear falling just before the living-room door slams open.

Willow, previously not a believer, says the place is sucking the energy out of him. He sleeps up to eighteen hours at a stretch. He is looking for another home.

Source: https://www.dailystar.co.uk/real-life/dad-flee-haunted-flat-cctv-36869391

Caribou County, Idaho, near the community of Bench, roughly 170 miles east of Twin Falls. Friday evening, September 4, 2026.

Two witnesses look up and see three triangular, multi-colored objects flying north, then yanking through multiple U-turns in a way one of them calls physically impossible.

One witness is a former soldier who served from 2003 to 2015. He hears jets at the same time. He says he knows what fighters sound like. The objects and the jets share the sky over coordinates he later gives as 42.47801, -111.58506.

They report it to NUFORC. Case #200684 becomes one of nineteen Idaho reports the center has worked in 2026. Three triangles. Jets. No official explanation on the page.

Source: https://983thesnake.com/ufo-sightings-idaho-military-jets-uaps/

Hunt County, Texas, about 50 miles northeast of Dallas near Greenville. Saturday, October 4, 2025, 7:09 p.m.

A farm family is out feeding the dogs on a seven-acre pasture when all four bolt toward the tree line, barking hard. Something steps out of the trees and starts cutting across the grass toward a pond at the back of the property. Upright. Moving fast without looking like it is running.

The dogs reach it, go silent, and turn back to the house. Three witnesses scramble for phones. They get photos and a short video of a distant dark figure striding across the open ground. As it nears the pond, witnesses say it drops to all fours and keeps going.

The neighbors who own the land find no tracks the next morning. The ground is too dry. BFRO holds the report for months, waiting on the landowner's permission for a size-comparison walk, then finally posts it with the video.

Source: https://www.bfro.net/GDB/show_report.asp?id=79293

Answer: C) Loch Ness Monster

Nessie is the long-necked, humped shape said to haunt Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands, and sightings exploded after the story hit the papers in 1933. The oldest monster tale tied to the area is far older: Adomnán's Life of St. Columba says the saint turned back a "water beast" in the River Ness with the sign of the cross around AD 565.

How'd you do?
posts.headline: Answer: C) Loch Ness Monster

Have you heard of the Book of Giants?

Top 5 things to know about the Dead Sea Scrolls' lost giant story:

1) The Book of Giants is an ancient text that expands Genesis 6:1-4, the story of the sons of God and the daughters of men, much like the Book of Enoch does.
2) Its giants are the offspring of the Watchers, and in it God sends dreams to two giant brothers named Ohyah and Hahyah.
3) The giants send one of their own, Mahway, to Enoch to interpret the dreams, and Enoch answers with tablets announcing God's judgment.
4) For centuries it was known only through Manichaean fragments found at Turfan in western China, until Aramaic copies were identified among the Dead Sea Scrolls.
5) The Qumran fragments even name Gilgamesh and Humbaba among the giants.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Giants
posts.headline: Have you heard of the Book of Giants?

posts.text:
Have you heard of the tsuchinoko?

Top 5 things to know about Japan's fat-bodied jumping snake:

1) Tsuchinoko means "child of hammer," a snake-like cryptid from western Japan also called bachi hebi in the northeast.
2) Witnesses describe a snake about 12 to 31 inches long with a thick central body, viper-like fangs, and venom.
3) It supposedly jumps about three feet, and some stories say it can bite its own tail and roll like a wheel.
4) Folklore adds that it can talk, likes to lie, and has a taste for alcohol.
5) In 1988 the village of Shimokitayama offered 1 million yen for one caught alive. About 200 people searched. None was found, and the village opened a Tsuchinoko Park in 2023.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsuchinoko
posts.headline: Have you heard of the tsuchinoko?

posts.text:
Have you heard of the kelpie?

Top 5 things to know about Scotland's shape-shifting water horse:

1) The kelpie is the most common water spirit in Scottish folklore, a shape-shifter said to haunt rivers, streams, and lochs.
2) It usually appears as a gray or white horse, but it can take human form.
3) Some accounts say it keeps its hooves even in human shape, which linked it to the devil in Christian imagination. Robert Burns nods to it in his 1786 "Address to the Devil."
4) Almost every sizable body of water in Scotland has a kelpie story, and many see the legend as a warning to keep children away from dangerous water.
5) Today two 100-foot steel horse heads called The Kelpies, completed in 2013, tower over the canal at Falkirk.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelpie
posts.headline: Have you heard of the kelpie?

posts.text:
Have you heard of Og of Bashan?

Top 5 things to know about the last king of the giants:

1) Og was the Amorite king of Bashan, east of the Jordan, and the Bible calls him the last survivor of the Rephaim, the giants.
2) His kingdom held sixty cities fortified with high walls and barred gates, with Ashtaroth as a capital.
3) Moses and Israel defeated Og and his army at Edrei, told in Numbers 21 and Deuteronomy 3.
4) Deuteronomy 3:11 says his iron bed was nine cubits long and four wide, about 13.5 by 6 feet, and could still be seen in Rabbah of the Ammonites.
5) Later tradition kept his legend growing: Arabic sources call him ʿŪj ibn ʿAnāq, "Og son of Anaq."

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Og
posts.headline: Have you heard of Og of Bashan?

posts.text:
Have you heard of the Yowie?

Top 5 things to know about Australia's hairy man of the bush:

1) The Yowie is Australia's big hairy biped, with roots in Aboriginal oral history, especially in the eastern states.
2) Witnesses describe it walking upright, ape-like and covered in hair, standing roughly 7 to 12 feet tall with a wide, flat nose.
3) In 1875, Rev. William Ridley recorded "Yō-wī" among the Gamilaraay people as a spirit that roams the earth at night.
4) In 1882, naturalist Henry James McCooey claimed he saw a tailless "indigenous ape" with long black hair on the New South Wales south coast.
5) Reported Yowie footprints are far bigger than a human's, but the tracks don't agree on shape or even toe count.

Learn more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yowie
posts.headline: Have you heard of the Yowie?

South of Socorro, New Mexico. April 24, 1964, around 5:45 p.m. Police Sergeant Lonnie Zamora is chasing a speeder when he hears a roar and sees a flame in the sky to the southwest. Thinking a dynamite shack blew, he breaks off the chase. Down in an arroyo he spots a shiny, aluminum-white object shaped like an O, at first sure it is an overturned car. Beside it stand two figures in white overalls, like small adults or large kids. Then another roar. A blue and orange flame flares underneath, and the object rises and speeds away. Officers find smoldering brush and shallow holes in the ground. Project Blue Book files it as unknown.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonnie_Zamora_incident

Lawndale, Illinois, along the open fields near Kickapoo Creek. Evening of July 25, 1977. Ten-year-old Marlon Lowe is playing outside his family's home when two giant birds pass overhead. Coal black. Long necks ringed in white. Long curled beaks. Wingspans of ten feet or more. One suddenly swoops down, grabs the boy, and carries him a few feet. His mother screams. The bird drops him. Seven witnesses, and every one describes exactly the same thing. From the start, the birds are compared to Andean condors, which do carry that white neck ring. Andean condors live in South America. Not over central Illinois.

Source: https://cryptomundo.com/cryptozoo-news/lawndale07/

Wotton-under-Edge, Gloucestershire, England. Friday, August 28, 2026. Inside the Ancient Ram Inn, a 12th-century former tavern often called England's most haunted building, a cleaner is polishing a wooden cot in the children's playroom the staff call the Den. Then a baby pram in the room starts rolling. Slowly. Toward her. She steps back, pushes it back into place, and says quietly, "It's alright, I know you're there." The CCTV caught all of it. Skeptics blame an uneven floor. A manager says she jumped on those boards herself and the pram never budged. Guests report hearing children giggling through the building. Children's bones were reportedly unearthed at the Ram decades ago.

Source: https://www.dailystar.co.uk/news/latest-news/pram-moves-englands-most-haunted-37697516

Coeur d'Alene, Idaho. About 2 p.m., full daylight. A married couple looks up and finds something enormous hovering over the tree line. Rectangular. They put it at 300 to 400 feet across. Lights in multiple colors, blinking on two separate sides of it. Just a slab of something hanging above the pines in the middle of the afternoon. They catch it on cellphone video and report it to NUFORC on August 14. Case #200185 becomes the 17th Idaho report the center takes up this year. The video is on file. The object still has no name. And it is not the first one over Coeur d'Alene in 2026.

Source: https://kezj.com/ufo-reports-idaho-2026/

Onondaga County, New York. August 10, 2026, about 1 p.m. A hiker in her 50s has a remote glacial pond and bog all to herself on her day off. Empty parking lot. She raises her phone for a wide shot of the water, then catches movement to her left. About 240 feet out, something is wading along the edge. Her first thought: a naked man. She takes a couple of photos. On the second one, it snaps its head around and looks right at her. She turns and walks away. When she circles back to the shoreline, nobody is there. Just a sign: no swimming or wading. At home she studies the photos. It looks inhuman.

Source: https://www.bfro.net/GDB/show_report.asp?id=82485
